## What managing Glenview takes.

### The Glen and master-planned communities
The redevelopment of the former Glenview Naval Air Station created The Glen, townhome and condominium communities with layered master-and-sub-association structures around Gallery Park and The Glen Town Center. We manage within exactly these frameworks, keeping every sub-association's budget and interests distinct.

### Townhome capital cycles
Glenview's townhome associations, from 1970s-era communities to newer construction, are aging into the expensive decade: roofing, siding, and private-road replacement. Our reserve planning and capital project oversight carry no separate management fee, which matters when the project is seven figures.

### Village standards, commuter rhythms
With two Metra stations, top-rated schools, and some of the North Shore's highest property values, Glenview owners expect immaculate common areas, reliable snow and landscape contracts, and portal-first communication that respects a commuter's schedule.

### Does CenterPoint manage associations in Glenview?
Yes. CenterPoint Association Management provides condominium, HOA, and townhome association management in Glenview (ZIP 60025, 60026). Every association gets a dedicated manager, monthly financial reporting, and board support grounded in Illinois association law.

### How much does association management cost in Glenview?
Management starts at $20 per unit per month, quoted as a flat monthly fee based on your association's size, building systems, financial complexity, and service scope. It is never a percentage of your budget. See [pricing](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/pricing) for what drives the fee.

### How does a Glenview association switch to CenterPoint?
Plan on a managed 30 to 60 day transition after your board gives notice under its current contract. We retrieve records from the outgoing manager, set up banking and vendor relationships, notify owners, and open board and resident access. ### How should a Glenview board compare management companies?
Compare at least three firms on the same terms: an active Illinois community association management firm license, a licensed manager, a flat monthly fee in writing, after-hours emergency coverage, and a written transition plan.
